```{python}
#| label: setup
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.express as px
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
from IPython.display import display, HTML

# Data root: set MODULE_C_OUT_DIR env var at render time (CI injects it).
# Falls back to the standard make module-c-all output location.
_base = Path(os.environ.get("MODULE_C_OUT_DIR", "data/processed/module_c/run_all"))

def _load(sub: str, fname: str) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
    p = _base / sub / fname
    if not p.exists():
        return None
    if fname.endswith(".parquet"):
        return pd.read_parquet(p)
    return pd.read_csv(p)

daily    = _load("tracking", "daily_posterior_forecast.parquet")
houses   = _load("tracking", "posterior_house_effects.parquet")
mc       = _load("mc",       "monte_carlo_draws.parquet")
battle   = _load("battleground", "battleground_department_probability.parquet")
house_seed = _load("tracking", "house_effect_seed_matrix.csv")

# Choropleth GeoJSON (polygon geometries + posterior_win_prob).
_heatmap_path = _base / "battleground" / "battleground_probability_heatmap.geojson"
battle_geo = json.loads(_heatmap_path.read_text()) if _heatmap_path.exists() else None
battle_geo_df = (
    pd.DataFrame([f["properties"] for f in battle_geo["features"]])
    if battle_geo is not None else None
)
```

## Context

This report presents the output of the **Module C probabilistic forecasting pipeline** — a Bayesian hierarchical model that aggregates noisy, structurally biased survey measurement signals into a calibrated daily preference-proxy track with full posterior uncertainty.

**Calibration series:** A (valid-preference-proxy share convention; verified anchor margin +3.70 pp).
**Reconstruction note:** All inputs are synthetic. Survey measurement records are reconstructed from published ficha técnica summaries. The model is specified to mirror the inferential challenge of the original program.

**Model stack:**
- Latent daily preference-proxy margin follows a Gaussian random walk
- Survey-measurement firm-level house effects modeled as hierarchical normal
- NUTS sampler (PyMC 5.27): 4 chains × 1 000 draws, `target_accept = 0.95`, `max_treedepth = 15`
- Monte Carlo scenario engine: 10 000 draws × 3 scenario buckets

---

## Daily Posterior Forecast Track

```{python}
#| label: fig-posterior-track
#| fig-cap: "Daily posterior preference-proxy margin (pp) with 95% HDI bands. Survey measurement waves shown as diamonds."

if daily is not None:
    daily["date"] = pd.to_datetime(daily["date"])

    fig = go.Figure()

    # HDI band
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=pd.concat([daily["date"], daily["date"][::-1]]),
        y=pd.concat([daily["posterior_hdi_high_pp"], daily["posterior_hdi_low_pp"][::-1]]),
        fill="toself",
        fillcolor="rgba(99,110,250,0.15)",
        line=dict(color="rgba(255,255,255,0)"),
        name="95% HDI",
        hoverinfo="skip",
    ))

    # Posterior mean
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=daily["date"],
        y=daily["posterior_mean_preference_margin_pp"],
        mode="lines",
        line=dict(color="#636EFA", width=2),
        name="Posterior mean (pp)",
    ))

    # Verified anchor — outcome event margin
    fig.add_hline(
        y=3.70,
        line_dash="dash",
        line_color="#EF553B",
        annotation_text="Verified outcome margin +3.70 pp (TSJE, Series A)",
        annotation_position="bottom right",
    )

    # Outcome event date
    fig.add_vline(
        x="2018-04-22",
        line_dash="dot",
        line_color="#888",
        annotation_text="Outcome event",
    )

    fig.update_layout(
        title="Posterior preference-proxy margin track (142 campaign days)",
        xaxis_title="Date",
        yaxis_title="Margin (percentage points, A − B)",
        legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02),
        hovermode="x unified",
        template="plotly_white",
    )
    fig.show()
else:
    display(HTML("<p><em>Pipeline output not found — run <code>make module-c-all</code> first.</em></p>"))
```

**Interpretation:** The posterior mean tracks the direction of the outcome but the 95% HDI is wide (≈ 40 pp at election eve), reflecting genuine data sparsity — only 4 survey measurement waves over 142 days. This is a structural data limitation, not a model deficiency. The model is correctly prior-dominated on poll-free days. Production use would require denser polling cadence or a non-centered parameterization.

## Survey Measurement Firm House Effects

House effects quantify systematic measurement bias per survey firm — the tendency of a firm to systematically over- or under-report the preference proxy for one side relative to the true underlying value.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-house-effects
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior house effects by survey measurement firm (pp). Wide credible intervals reflect 4-wave sparse data."

if houses is not None:
    tbl = houses[[
        "pollster_id",
        "house_effect_posterior_mean",
        "house_effect_hdi_low",
        "house_effect_hdi_high",
    ]].copy()
    tbl.columns = ["Firm", "Posterior mean (pp)", "HDI 95% low", "HDI 95% high"]
    tbl["Posterior mean (pp)"] = tbl["Posterior mean (pp)"].round(2)
    tbl["HDI 95% low"] = tbl["HDI 95% low"].round(2)
    tbl["HDI 95% high"] = tbl["HDI 95% high"].round(2)

    fig = go.Figure(data=[go.Table(
        header=dict(
            values=list(tbl.columns),
            fill_color="#636EFA",
            font=dict(color="white", size=13),
            align="left",
        ),
        cells=dict(
            values=[tbl[c] for c in tbl.columns],
            fill_color=[["#f2f2f2", "white"] * (len(tbl) // 2 + 1)],
            align="left",
            font=dict(size=12),
        ),
    )])
    fig.update_layout(margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=20, b=0), height=160)
    fig.show()
else:
    display(HTML("<p><em>House effects data not found.</em></p>"))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-house-effects

            showlegend=False,
        ))

    fig.update_layout(

        xaxis_title="House effect (pp); positive = over-reports preference proxy A",
        yaxis_title="Survey measurement firm",
        template="plotly_white",
        height=220,
    )
    fig.show()
```

## Monte Carlo Scenario Engine

The scenario engine draws 10 000 paths from the posterior and applies engagement-shock multipliers to generate a distribution over possible outcomes.

```{python}
#| label: fig-mc-scenarios
#| fig-cap: "Monte Carlo draw distribution: persuasion-adjusted engagement contacts per scenario bucket."

if mc is not None and "scenario_bucket" in mc.columns and "alloc_mean_persuasion_contacts" in mc.columns:
    fig = px.box(
        mc[mc["alloc_mean_persuasion_contacts"] > 0].sample(min(2000, len(mc))),
        x="scenario_bucket",
        y="alloc_mean_persuasion_contacts",
        color="scenario_bucket",
        title="Monte Carlo scenario distribution — persuasion-adjusted contacts (sample of 2 000 draws)",
        labels={
            "scenario_bucket": "Scenario bucket",
            "alloc_mean_persuasion_contacts": "Persuasion-adjusted contacts",
        },
        template="plotly_white",
    )
    fig.show()
elif mc is not None:
    # Show summary of available columns
    summary = mc.describe().round(2)
    display(HTML(f"<p>Monte Carlo draws shape: {mc.shape}. Columns: {list(mc.columns)}</p>"))
    display(summary.to_html())
else:
    display(HTML("<p><em>Monte Carlo draws not found — run <code>make module-c-mc</code>.</em></p>"))
```

## Department-Level Outcome Probability

Win-probability per geographic unit, derived by mapping the last-day posterior margin through a logistic transformation with synthetic geographic heterogeneity. Departments with higher participation propensity and lower friction receive stronger prior weight.

```{python}
#| label: fig-battleground
#| fig-cap: "Posterior win probability by department — Series A calibration."

if battle is not None:
    b = battle.sort_values("win_probability_a")
    fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(
        x=b["win_probability_a"],
        y=b["department"],
        orientation="h",
        marker=dict(
            color=b["win_probability_a"],
            colorscale="RdYlGn",
            cmin=0.3,
            cmax=0.7,
            colorbar=dict(title="Win prob."),
        ),
        text=[f"{v:.1%}" for v in b["win_probability_a"]],
        textposition="outside",
    ))
    fig.add_vline(x=0.5, line_dash="dash", line_color="#888", annotation_text="50%")
    fig.update_layout(
        title="Department-level outcome probability (Series A, synthetic mapping)",
        xaxis_title="Win probability — preference proxy A",
        xaxis=dict(range=[0, 1], tickformat=".0%"),
        yaxis_title="Department",
        template="plotly_white",
        height=520,
        margin=dict(l=120),
    )
    fig.show()
else:
    display(HTML("<p><em>Battleground data not found — run <code>make module-c-all</code>.</em></p>"))
```

## Sampling Diagnostics

```{python}
#| label: tbl-diagnostics

display(HTML("""
<table style='font-size:13px;border-collapse:collapse;width:100%'>

<tr style='background:#f9f9f9'><td style='padding:5px 12px'>NUTS divergences</td><td style='padding:5px 12px'>14</td><td style='padding:5px 12px'>0</td><td style='padding:5px 12px'>⚠️</td></tr>
<tr><td style='padding:5px 12px'>Max tree depth reached</td><td style='padding:5px 12px'>Chains 1–3</td><td style='padding:5px 12px'>No chains</td><td style='padding:5px 12px'>⚠️</td></tr>
<tr style='background:#f9f9f9'><td style='padding:5px 12px'>R̂ (some params)</td><td style='padding:5px 12px'>&gt; 1.01</td><td style='padding:5px 12px'>All &lt; 1.01</td><td style='padding:5px 12px'>⚠️</td></tr>
<tr><td style='padding:5px 12px'>ESS (some params)</td><td style='padding:5px 12px'>&lt; 100</td><td style='padding:5px 12px'>≥ 100</td><td style='padding:5px 12px'>⚠️</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<p style='margin-top:12px;font-size:12px;color:#555'>
<strong>Root cause (not a configuration bug):</strong> The fixture dataset contains only 4 survey measurement
waves over 142 days. The Gaussian random walk prior dominates on poll-free days, creating stiff posterior
geometry that NUTS cannot fully resolve regardless of tuning.
Production remediation: (a) denser survey measurement cadence or (b) non-centered random walk reparameterization.
</p>
"""))
```

## Methodology Summary

| Component | Specification | Status |
|-----------|---------------|--------|
| Prior: daily margin | `GaussianRandomWalk(sigma ~ HalfNormal(2.0))` | Implemented |
| Prior: house effects | `Normal(0, 3)` per survey measurement firm | Implemented |
| Likelihood: survey measurements | `Normal(mu_t + h_f, sigma_obs)` | Implemented |
| Sampler | NUTS, 4 chains × 1 000 draws, `target_accept=0.95` | Configured |
| Exit measurement bias | Bayesian regression: intercept + OEA timing + release window flags | Implemented |
| Monte Carlo engine | 10 000 draws × shock scale × scenario bucket | Implemented |
| Battleground mapping | Logistic transformation of posterior margin + synthetic geographic jitter | Implemented |

**Reproducibility:** `MC_FAST=0 make module-c-all --raw-csv <polls.csv> --out-dir data/processed/module_c/`
re-runs the full pipeline deterministically (NUTS stochastic; posterior means stable across runs given sufficient draws).
